products.aiPlanner.metaDescription: Motir AI Planner asks until it is clear what you are building, then drafts the whole plan: every piece of work, in order, with who does it. Nothing starts until you approve it.
products.aiPlanner.headline: First the what. Then the whole plan.
products.aiPlanner.lede: Describe what you want to build. The planner asks until it is clear what you mean, because it won't plan a guess. Then it reads what already exists and drafts the whole plan: every piece of work, in the order it has to happen, with who does it. Nothing starts until you approve it.
products.aiPlanner.steps.headline: It thinks it through with you
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.0.title: Asks until it's clear
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.0.body: If it isn't yet clear what you're building, it asks. It won't plan until it knows.
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.1.title: Reads what exists
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.1.body: Your repositories, documents and board, or a project you bring from Jira, Linear or Plane. It plans from where you are, not from a blank page.
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.2.title: Drafts the whole plan
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.2.body: Every piece of work from the big goals down to the small steps, each with who does it and what it waits on.
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.3.title: Checks its own work
products.aiPlanner.steps.items.3.body: Every plan is checked before you see it, so what reaches you is a plan that can be built.
products.aiPlanner.gate.headline: You approve the plan
products.aiPlanner.gate.body: Nothing reaches the board until you say so. Ask for changes in plain words: move this later, split that, drop the export. Each round is a new turn, and the plan keeps every version and the reason it changed.
products.aiPlanner.gate.motirPlans: Create an account to see what Motir planned for itself
products.aiPlanner.holds.headline: Everything the work needs
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.0.title: The whole tree
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.0.body: Epics, stories, tasks and subtasks, from the goal down to the step.
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.1.title: Who does it
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.1.body: Each work item goes to an agent or to a person. Work only a person can do is a manual task.
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.2.title: The order
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.2.body: What waits on what, so each piece starts the moment it can.
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.3.title: The difficulty
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.3.body: A level on every work item, so it runs on a model that fits it.
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.4.title: The kind of work
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.4.body: Code, design, tests, documents, research, review: each kind is marked.
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.5.title: The schedule
products.aiPlanner.holds.items.5.body: Once you approve: sprints, a backlog and a roadmap.
products.aiPlanner.learns.headline: It learns from every mistake
products.aiPlanner.learns.body: When an agent can't build what the plan asked for, Motir first checks whether the plan was wrong or was changed after you approved it. A real planning mistake becomes a lesson, or strengthens one. Every new plan reads the lessons first, and a lesson that hasn't been needed for 90 days retires.

products.aiDebugging.describe.headline: Say what's broken. Motir AI traces it.
products.aiDebugging.describe.body: Describe the bug in your own words, or report it and hand it over. Motir AI reads your code and your plan, names the likely cause, and checks for a card that already covers it. It writes one thing and says exactly what: a new bug in Triage with the diagnosis, or the diagnosis added to the card that already tracks it. If it can't trace the bug to the code, it writes nothing.
products.aiDebugging.production.headline: Errors arrive as bugs, with the evidence

products.agentFleet.lede: Motir's hosted agents take every work item that is ready and work them at the same time, each on a fresh machine with its own branch and pull request. Start them yourself, or let Motir Project Manager keep them busy, and the project moves on every front at once.
products.agentFleet.parallel.headline: One machine for every ready work item
products.agentFleet.parallel.body: Everything that can start, starts. Each run claims its work item, so no two agents ever take the same one, and works it on a machine of its own. A story runs its pieces in the order they depend on each other. The more work is ready, the more runs at once.
products.agentFleet.pm.headline: Motir Project Manager keeps the fleet busy
products.agentFleet.pm.body: Hand the project to Motir Project Manager and it starts a run the moment a work item is ready, picks the model, and brings you only what needs your decision: the pull requests, the designs, the plans.
products.agentFleet.models.eyebrow: The right model for each job
products.agentFleet.models.headline: Every work item has a difficulty. It picks the model.
products.agentFleet.models.body: The planner gives every task, subtask and bug a difficulty: how hard the work is to get right, not how big it is. A one-line change to lock ordering can be high while a large rename is trivial. The fleet reads it to choose the model, so a rename doesn't pay for the strongest model and a data migration never runs on the cheapest.

products.agentFleet.models.items.0.body: Mechanical work with an unambiguous spec: a rename, a copy change, a config flip. Runs on a faster, cheaper model.
products.agentFleet.models.items.1.title: Low
products.agentFleet.models.items.1.body: Routine work that follows a pattern the code already has, like a new field through an existing form. Runs on a faster, cheaper model.
products.agentFleet.models.items.2.title: Medium
products.agentFleet.models.items.2.body: Real design choices across several files or services, or a bug whose cause isn't known yet. Runs on the strongest model.
products.agentFleet.models.items.3.title: High
products.agentFleet.models.items.3.body: Work where a subtle mistake is costly: concurrency, security, a migration on live data. Runs on the strongest model.

howItWorks.lede: Every Motir project runs through the same instrument. The modules are Motir and its agents. The knobs and switches are yours: nothing moves forward until a person turns them.

howItWorks.toyDesc: A small plastic gadget with a single knob: type a prompt and out comes a heap of files, tangled in imports, with a circular import among them. howItWorks.rackTitle: The Motir workflow as a rack of modules
howItWorks.rackDesc: Your idea is patched into the planner, then into a knob where you approve the plan, then the board, then an agent run, then a knob where you review and merge, then Done. Manual tasks go from the board to Done. An agent run can log a bug it finds into the Bugs folder and keep going. A repair module loops failed runs back into the agent run. A learning loop runs from the agent run through a verdict, a re-plan and the lesson library back into the planner. A memory bank along the bottom holds designs, decisions, docs, lessons, run history, revisions and who decided what. A switch on the rack flips between vibe coding, which keeps only your idea and the agent run, and vibing the project, which uses every module.
howItWorks.schematicTitle: Motir's architecture as a circuit schematic
howItWorks.schematicDesc: The services behind Motir drawn as components joined by signal lines. In the public zone: motir.co, the design system package, the agent shell relay, motir-core (web and REST API, the MCP server, sign-in, and the worker with its job queue) and motir-ai, the planner. In the private zone: motir-gateway, which meters every model call, and the code graph service. In the fleet: the agent host, the agent runner, the index runner and the CI runner, all booted on demand. In the data zone: Postgres and the file store. Outside: your browser, your own agent connected over MCP, the payments provider, the model providers and your code host.

howItWorks.modules.0.label: [01] AI planning
howItWorks.modules.0.title: From a prompt to a plan
howItWorks.modules.0.paras.0: Start with a sentence, a repository, or an import from Jira, Linear or Plane. The planner reads what exists, including a code graph of your repositories, and asks follow-up questions where the request is ambiguous.
howItWorks.modules.0.paras.1: It drafts epics, stories, tasks and subtasks, each with a type, an executor, a size and its `blocked_by` edges. `validate_plan` checks the tree before you see it.
howItWorks.modules.1.label: [02] You · plan gate
howItWorks.modules.1.title: You approve the plan
howItWorks.modules.1.paras.0: Nothing lands on the board until a person approves the plan. Ask for changes in plain words; each round is a new turn, and the plan's history keeps every version and why it changed.
howItWorks.modules.2.label: [03] Work items
howItWorks.modules.2.title: The board
howItWorks.modules.2.paras.0: The approved plan becomes work items with sprints, a backlog and a roadmap. Each work item's executor is `agent` or `human`.
howItWorks.modules.2.paras.1: Manual tasks (an account, a secret, a DNS record, a release sign-off) are walked through one step at a time by `motir guide`.
howItWorks.modules.3.label: [04] Agent run
howItWorks.modules.3.title: Agents build
howItWorks.modules.3.paras.0: An agent takes the next ready work item (`motir next` or `motir run <KEY>`), claims it, builds on its own branch and opens one pull request per repository, linked to the work item.
howItWorks.modules.3.paras.1: A bug it finds outside its own work item doesn't stop the run: the agent root-causes it, files it with `motir log bug` into the Bugs folder as a work item of its own, and keeps going.
howItWorks.modules.3.paras.2: Each run records the agent harness, the model, every step and the outcome. Agents connect over MCP, on your machine or Motir's hosted agents.
howItWorks.modules.4.label: [05] You · merge gate
howItWorks.modules.4.title: You review and merge
howItWorks.modules.4.paras.0: The work item moves to `Implemented` and the agent publishes How to test. Stories get an acceptance video recorded in CI. You review, approve and merge; the merge closes the work item. Nothing reaches `Done` without a person.
howItWorks.modules.5.label: [06] Repair
howItWorks.modules.5.title: When runs break
howItWorks.modules.5.paras.0: A red or conflicting pull request is repaired on its own branch with `motir fix`, up to five attempts. A run that died (a laptop closed, a sandbox lost) is resumed with `motir continue` on the branch it left.
howItWorks.modules.5.paras.1: Bugs logged along the way wait in the Bugs folder; `motir fix bugs` works through them, oldest first.
howItWorks.modules.6.label: [07] Learning loop
howItWorks.modules.6.title: The planner learns
howItWorks.modules.6.paras.0: An agent that can't build a work item first asks whether it is still what the approved plan approved (`get_approved_shape_verdict`), so a later edit isn't blamed on the planner. If the plan was wrong, it is re-planned and the change is recorded with its reason.
howItWorks.modules.6.paras.1: The mistake becomes a lesson, or reinforces one; with no rule to cover it, a planning bug is filed. The next plan reads the lessons first. Lessons that don't recur for 90 days retire.
howItWorks.modules.7.label: [08] Memory
howItWorks.modules.7.title: The project remembers
howItWorks.modules.7.paras.0: Designs, decision pages, docs, lessons, plan revisions and every run's history live next to the work items. You, a new teammate or the next agent can pick the project up months later without anyone explaining it again.

builtByMotirPage.headline: How Motir builds Motir.
builtByMotirPage.lede: It sounds like a chicken-and-egg problem. It isn't. Motir started as a folder of prompts, and every feature it shipped became a tool for building the next one.

builtByMotirPage.lost.scenes.question: why this way?
builtByMotirPage.lost.headline: We vibe coded. The project fell apart.
builtByMotirPage.lost.body: Vibe coding made the code fast. But the further we got, the more of the project we lost — because a project is not only code.
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.0.title: A bug found, never tracked
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.0.body: Spotted in the middle of a session, forgotten by the end of it.
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.1.title: Too much at once
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.1.body: Five features in flight, and no way to tell which one to start next.
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.2.title: Tests that weren't there
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.2.body: Missing, or not up to the standard the rest of the code needed.
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.3.title: Decisions lost in a chat
builtByMotirPage.lost.items.3.body: Why something was built that way ended when the coding session did.
builtByMotirPage.missing.headline: Jira and Linear track work. We needed more.
builtByMotirPage.missing.body: We plugged our process into the project tools we knew. They held the tasks, but not the thing we were missing.
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.0.title: A plan before the code
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.0.body: An agent should start from a plan a person approved, not from a prompt.
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.1.title: Ready, or blocked by what
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.1.body: See which work can start now, and which waits — on exactly which other work.
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.2.title: Someone running the whole project
builtByMotirPage.missing.items.2.body: A project manager that oversees everything and puts it together, without being asked.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.headline: Every feature becomes the tool for the next.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.body: Motir didn't wait to be finished before it was used. Each feature it shipped replaced the scaffolding it was built with.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.0.title: motir-meta
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.0.body: An internal project: a set of prompts, a task list and a store of mistakes. It prompted a model to build Motir's first features.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.1.title: Work items
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.1.body: With work items shipped, Motir asked itself what to build next, not an outside tool.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.2.title: The MCP server
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.2.body: With the MCP shipped, those lookups became MCP calls, and status kept itself in sync.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.3.title: AI planning
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.3.body: With planning shipped, Motir planned its next features with its own planner.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.4.title: Agents and approvals
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.steps.4.body: Agents build Motir's work items; a person approves every plan and every merge.
builtByMotirPage.bootstrap.loop.2: Build the next one with it

howToUse.metaTitle: How to use Motir: one part, two, or all three
howToUse.metaDescription: Motir has three parts: a planner, the project management tool in the middle, and an agent runner. Use the middle with your own planner and agents over MCP, add the Motir planner, or let Motir run all three.
howToUse.headline: Use one part, two, or all three.
howToUse.lede: Motir has three parts. The project management tool sits in the middle and holds the plan. The planner plans into it. The agent runner takes tasks from it and builds them. Any part you'd rather run yourself, you can.
howToUse.parts.0.name: Motir AI Planner
howToUse.parts.0.body: Turns your idea into epics, stories and tasks, and files them into the project once you approve.
howToUse.parts.1.name: Motir Project Management
howToUse.parts.1.body: The board, backlog, sprints and roadmap. Every planner and every agent, yours or Motir's, works through it.
howToUse.parts.2.name: Motir Agent Fleet
howToUse.parts.2.body: Takes each ready task, runs an agent on it on its own machine, in parallel with the others, and opens the pull request.
howToUse.ways.0.label: 1 · Project management only
howToUse.ways.0.title: Your planner, your agents, Motir in the middle.
howToUse.ways.0.paras.0: Use Motir as the project management tool and keep everything around it your own.
howToUse.ways.0.paras.1: Planning over MCP stays open. Write your own planner, a script or an agent, and it files the plan into Motir with the same tools Motir's planner uses: `create_plan`, `add_plan_items` and `validate_plan`. Before Motir AI Planner was built, Motir planned itself this way too, with a script called plan.py.
howToUse.ways.0.paras.2: Your agents connect over MCP. Each one takes the next ready task with `claim_next_ready`, runs it, and reports back with `close_work_item_run`. Motir keeps track of who has which task and what shipped.

explainer.metaTitle: How the calculation works — Motir AI
explainer.metaDescription: Where Motir AI's credit estimate and the plan it recommends come from: what you enter, model categories, credits per item, the range, the plan ladder up to Host and the larger pool plans, and who pays for what.
explainer.headline: How the calculation works
explainer.lede: Where the credit estimate and the plan it recommends come from — the same figures the price page and the calculator use.
explainer.figuresUnavailableNote: Live figures are not available right now, so this page explains each step in words. The price page shows every plan with its price.
explainer.entryLink: Want to know where these numbers come from? <link>How the calculation works</link>
explainer.s1.title: What you enter
explainer.s1.ranges: Two ranges a month: items you plan in Motir, and items you run on Motir's runner.
explainer.s1.ownAgent: An item you run on your own agent — Claude Code, Codex — through Motir's MCP or CLI uses no running credits. If you run everything yourself, enter zero runs and you are quoted planning only.
explainer.s2.title: Model categories
explainer.s2.body: Planning and running each take a category, not a specific model. Example models come from Motir's live model list, so no model here is a promise.
explainer.s2.categoriesFigureFree: The category names come from Motir's live model list.
explainer.s2.split: Two or three selected categories share the estimate as you set them in the Calculator, starting even: 50/50 for two, 34/33/33 for three.
explainer.s3.title: Credits per item
explainer.s3.body: A reference amount of work per item, times the live price of the chosen model, times a lane factor for planning and for running. The reference is the typical work one item takes; it is not a price.
explainer.s3.laneFactors: Planning and running each carry their own lane factor.
explainer.s4.title: The range
explainer.s4.body: Real token use varies, so low items are counted at 1× and high items at 2×.
explainer.s4.caption: Always a range, never a single number.
explainer.s5.title: The recommendation
explainer.s5.body: The calculator recommends the cheapest of these plans that covers your high end. Each is a plan of its own.
explainer.s5.maxX2FigureFree: A plan of its own, twice Max's credits
explainer.s5.topUp: A small shortfall is covered by a top-up estimate at {price} for {credits} credits.
explainer.s5.topUpFigureFree: A small shortfall is covered by a top-up estimate at the catalog's top-up rate.
explainer.s5.largerBody: When your high end is past Max ×2 and a sensible top-up, the calculator offers a larger pool plan sized from your own estimate, on the same per-credit basis as the ladder, and you buy it yourself.
explainer.s5.largerFrom: Larger plans start from {credits} credits a month.
explainer.s5.largerFromFigureFree: Larger plans start well above Host's credits.
explainer.s6.title: Host, and what a plan includes beyond credits
explainer.s6.hostBody: A regular plan above Max ×2. You buy it from the price page; the calculator never recommends it, because what it buys is not only credits. A Host organization gets three AWS accounts of its own:
explainer.s6.accounts.0.name: Account 1
explainer.s6.accounts.1.name: Account 2
explainer.s6.accounts.2.name: Account 3
explainer.s6.accounts.2.use: Shared by indexing and hosted agents
explainer.s6.sharedFloor: Until AWS grants those accounts' capacity, a Host organization runs on Motir's shared capacity with Max's limits, and its admin sees each account's state.
explainer.s6.largerPlans: The larger pool plans start well above Host and also carry AWS accounts of their own.
explainer.s6.otherPlans: Every other plan runs on Motir's shared capacity, with how many agent runs and hosted agents it may have at once set by its plan.
explainer.s7.title: Who pays for what
explainer.s7.organization: Every AI plan — Standard, Pro, Max, Max ×2, Host and the larger pool plans — and every top-up belongs to the organization. Its credits are shared by the whole organization; an AI plan is not priced by how many people use it and has no quantity.
explainer.s7.includedSeat: Every AI plan includes one Motir seat at no charge.
explainer.s7.furtherSeats: Seats beyond the first are per user: each further person who uses Motir takes a seat at the Motir seat fee.
explainer.s7.noAiPlanSeats: An organization with no AI plan pays for every seat.
explainer.s8.title: Changing plan mid-period
explainer.s8.upBody: You pay the price difference for the days left in the period, not a full new price, and receive the matching extra credits and code-graph index allowance for those days.
explainer.s8.upRenewal: Every renewal after that grants the new plan's full pool. An upgrade also clears a downgrade you scheduled earlier.
explainer.s8.downBody: Takes effect at the end of the current period, with no refund and no change to the credits or allowance you already hold. You keep your current plan until then.
explainer.s8.downClear: Upgrading again before then clears the scheduled downgrade.
explainer.s8.billingNote: The exact amount of an upgrade is shown to the owner on the billing page before they confirm.
explainer.s9.title: What changes the answer
explainer.s9.body: A gateway price change or a retired model changes the estimate, with no release of Motir.
explainer.s10.title: Invoices, security and SSO
explainer.s10.body: Standard Stripe invoicing. For security or SSO questions, <link>contact us</link>.
